promises.title: build primary healthcare centers in all wards
promises.promise_blog:
Too many communities grapple with delayed treatment, unaffordable travel to urban hospitals, and avoidable fatalities. Primary healthcare is the frontline of wellbeing—where immunisations begin, antenatal care finds its rhythm, and malaria meets its match. By placing centres in every ward, the government reaffirms health as a civic right, not a privilege of geography.

It strengthens the social contract, demonstrating that leadership sees every ward not as a data point, but as a community of lives that matter. It decentralises care, ensuring that each citizen has access to the primary point of care, boosts early detection of illnesses, and relieves pressure on tertiary institutions. More than anything, it says: “We are near, we are responsive, and we are accountable.”

The policy is clear, the demand is loud, and the rationale is undeniable. Building primary healthcare centres is humane. Let each ward become a sanctuary of health and a testament to governance that heals.
promises.description: Build Primary Healthcare Centers in All Wards to improve healthcare access.

promises.title: Build udomi-uwessa teaching hospital
promises.promise_blog:
The planned Udomi-Uwessa Teaching Hospital represents a transformative step in healthcare infrastructure in the region, poised to deliver comprehensive tertiary health care while advancing medical education and research. Strategically sited to serve underserved districts, the facility will combine state-of-the-art diagnostic imaging and laboratory sciences with fully equipped operating theatres and intensive care units. By integrating modern medicine, emergency response units, and outpatient services, the hospital addresses critical gaps in clinical services and supports interdisciplinary collaboration among physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and allied health professionals.

Emphasis on evidence-based medicine and clinical training drives the establishment of robust residency programs in internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, and obstetrics. Dedicated wings for pathology, radiology, and pharmacology research foster an environment where resident physicians and medical students engage in epidemiology studies and translational medicine projects. The inclusion of simulation labs and telemedicine suites enhances skill acquisition, ensuring that the next generation of healthcare providers is well-versed in patient safety, infection control, and critical care protocols.

Establishing Udomi-Uwessa Teaching Hospital is imperative to strengthen tertiary health care capacity, drive innovation in medicine, and cultivate a skilled healthcare workforce. This institution will bridge service gaps, accelerate improvements in life expectancy, and uphold health equity—fulfilling an urgent need for a dedicated center of excellence in medical education and patient care.
promises.description: Build udomi-uwessa teaching hospital

promises.title: Establish business incubation centers across three senatorial zones
promises.promise_blog:
What if the next game-changing startup only needs four walls, fast Wi-Fi, and someone in its corner? Now, how more beautiful would three state-of-the-art centres—one in each senatorial zone— be? Each offering spaces where business ideas can be nurtured into implementation through proper mentorship and legal support. By establishing Business Incubation Centres in each senatorial zone, the government would be providing business startups with the runway they deserve—turning sparks into scales and hustle into impact.

 

These centres will be more than consultation desks and conference rooms. They’ll be ecosystems of legal clinics, pitch practice, and peer collaboration—where local founders learn to navigate funding landscapes, refine their value propositions, and grow networks that outlast their first prototypes.

 

This initiative bridges ambition and opportunity, forging economic arteries that pump talent from every ward into the heart of the Edo marketplace. Plans ought to be in place, funds secured, partners locked in. Let the doors open and the next wave of entrepreneurs prove just how far support can take them.

promises.title: Revive the musical water fountain.
promises.promise_blog: The musical water fountain at Ring Road in Benin City once stood as a luminous symbol of urban enjoyment and public recreation, combining artistry with leisure in a way few landmarks can match. As night fell, streetlights lit up the square, inviting residents and visitors to pause, to marvel, and to share moments of communal delight. Over time, however, mechanical wear and inadequate maintenance relegated the fountain to silence and stillness. Its absence has left a void in the city’s heartscape—a missing piece of public recreation that once energized the cultural life of Benin. Moreover, the fountain served as an open-air stage for gatherings—families strolling beneath the spray, couples forging memories at its edge. As a fun spot, it encouraged social interactions, offering a shared point of reference that united diverse communities. In reviving the musical water fountain, Benin City has the opportunity to reanimate a vital source of recreation, to rekindle public affection, and to reaffirm the belief that beauty and ambience are indispensable to vibrant urban life.
promises.description: I will revive the musical water fountain.

promises.promise_blog:
Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State has pledged a transformative solution to the long-standing deterioration of the Auchi–Igarra–Ibillo Federal Road, a critical artery connecting Akoko‑Edo communities to the rest of Edo, Kogi, and Ondo states. Residents, particularly those engaged in cassava processing, quarrying, and trade, welcomed the development. They had long decried difficulties in transporting goods due to the road’s deplorable state. The contractor, after carrying out a thorough inspection, assured they would meet the high standards set by the governor .

Governor Okpebholo’s intervention signals a shift towards proactive governance in Edo State. By tackling this vital corridor, his administration aims to boost economic activity, enhance connectivity, and restore safety for commuters and businesses alike.

promises.title: Establish the edo state security fund
promises.promise_blog:
The rising wave of violent crime, kidnappings, and communal clashes all boil down to one thing: current security infrastructure is overwhelmed, underfunded, understaffed, and outgunned by criminals. Without drastic intervention, this crisis will worsen. Communities live in fear, businesses operate under siege, and families mourn preventable losses. 

The establishment of the State Security Fund is the lifeline the good people of Edo state desperately need to see. This fund will provide critical resources for modern policing equipment, advanced surveillance technology, and specialized training for security personnel. It will empower local vigilante networks with legal backing and logistical support, bridging the gap where federal forces fall short. Most importantly, it ensures rapid response capabilities to save lives before tragedies occur.  

The cost of inaction far outweighs the investment required. Every day without this fund means more avoidable bloodshed, more abandoned farms and markets, and more economic paralysis.
promises.description: Establish the Edo State Security Fund to finance security operations, including equipment and logistics.

promises.title: Upgrade the Edo Broadcasting Service (EBS) station.
promises.promise_blog:
In its current state, the Edo Broadcasting Service station struggles with epileptic power supply, poor access roads, and inadequate digital infrastructure—limitations that undermine its role as a vital communication channel for Edo State. When sound quality falters and coverage gaps persist, information spread slows, and civic engagements can not be had. 

A failure to modernize also weakens the state's capacity for promoting public welfare. Health advisories, educational programs, and critical policy updates demand clear, uninterrupted broadcasts; outdated equipment simply can’t meet these imperatives. At the same time, opportunities for advertising revenue remain untapped, as private partners look elsewhere for high-quality production and measurable audience insights.  

A targeted investment in digital transmission and streaming equipment, backup power, and infrastructure would not merely patch weaknesses; it would reposition EBS as a forward-looking public service. Such an overhaul is essential if the station is to fulfill its promise of fostering civic engagement through live call-ins, social media integration, listener polls—that obsolete systems cannot support.
promises.description: I promise to upgrade the Edo Broadcasting Service (EBS) station.

promises.title: Rebuild Oluku Market
promises.promise_blog:
Oluku Market is located along the Benin–Lagos Road in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of Edo State. The market serves traders and customers in the surrounding communities, providing a place for commercial activities and a source of livelihood for many households.


On October 15, 2026, a petrol tanker incident followed by an explosion and fire destroyed shops and goods at the market, leaving traders facing significant losses. Reports indicated that traders were unable to salvage much of their merchandise before the fire spread. The incident also resulted in burn injuries, with victims receiving treatment at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH).


Following the incident, Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo visited the affected market on October 16, 2026, to assess the damage. During the visit, he pledged to rebuild Oluku Market and support traders who lost their shops and goods, assuring them that his administration would not abandon them. He also visited injured victims receiving treatment at UBTH.


The promise is significant because rebuilding the market could help restore commercial activity and enable affected traders to recover their livelihoods.
promises.description: Gov Okpebholo promised to rebuild the Oluku market following the fire incident that happened in October, 2026

This initiative aligns with his broader vision of enhancing human capital development and preparing young people for future opportunities.

Stakeholders in the education sector have welcomed the plan, noting that if fulfilled, it will not only raise the quality of education but also create employment for qualified graduates. The promise represents a key test of the new administration’s commitment to addressing structural gaps in Edo State’s education system.

Beyond physical structures, the provision of buses also addresses mobility challenges within and around the campus, improving accessibility for students and staff. Together, these interventions can enhance the overall academic environment, attract more students, and strengthen the university’s reputation as a competitive state-owned institution.


Ultimately, this promise reflects a broader commitment to investing in education as a driver of development, positioning Edo University, Iyamho for sustained growth and improved service delivery in the higher education sector.

promises.title: We will revive Edo Line
promises.promise_blog:
Edo Line was once a symbol of pride—moving people, connecting towns, and supporting the local economy. Over the years, however, this once-thriving state-owned transport company faded into dysfunction, leaving commuters with fewer options and rising transportation costs.

Now, Governor Monday Okpebholo is charting a new course with a bold promise: to revive Edo Line and restore its glory. This is more than a transport solution; it’s a commitment to accessible, affordable, and safe mobility for all Edo residents. The governor envisions a modern fleet, professionally managed operations, and a renewed focus on service delivery that meets today’s standards.

The plan includes overhauling the company’s infrastructure—repairing terminals, modernizing buses, retraining staff, and establishing digital ticketing systems. With improved management and strategic partnerships, Edo Line can regain the public’s trust and serve as a reliable option for students, workers, traders, and travelers.

This revival is also about economic stimulation. It promises job creation, ease of doing business, and improved interstate connectivity. By breathing new life into Edo Line, Governor Okpebholo is not just fixing a broken system—he’s restoring confidence in public transport and investing in the movement and dignity of the people.
promises.description: We will revive Edo Line

promises.title: Pave roads in ologbo dukedom
promises.promise_blog:
When the red soil of Ologbo Dukedom softens under rain, it carves raw wounds through villages—trenches where trucks vanish in mud, mothers cling to motorbike handrails, and schoolkids wade through floodwaters that erase roads. The consequences are relentless. Prices skyrocket as transport damages pile up. Investors abandon plans after a single punishing trip through the area. Basic needs—medical emergencies, construction deliveries, safe travel for the elderly—go unmet on these impassable dirt tracks.

 

Paving Ologbo’s roads is not luxury but life-saving. We've witnessed high allocations to projects that are less important and with little or no benefit to the collective wealth of the indigenous people of Benin.

 

The price of delay? Continued hardship, preventable deaths, and youth escaping this trap of geographic isolation. No more endless reports. No more empty assurances. The heavy equipment must arrive before another rainy season deepens the situation.
promises.description: Pave Roads in Ologbo Dukedom for improved infrastructure.
